# Open Question 9: Wire Diffeologies Generated by Motor Primitives

Date Added: May 4, 2026

### Context

The wire plane is the Euclidean plane equipped with the diffeology generated by *all* smooth curves. On this diffeological space, the equi-affine tensor underlying the Two-Thirds Power Law becomes a true covariant 3-tensor under the full diffeomorphism group — something the standard smooth structure cannot achieve. This is established in [1].

But the motor system does not use all curves. Experimental evidence suggests that complex movements are built from a discrete repertoire of motor primitives — elementary building blocks that can be combined and transformed according to syntactic rules [2]. In diffeological terms, a motor repertoire corresponds not to the full generating family, but to a proper subset of curves. This subset generates a sub-diffeology of the wire plane.

### The Problem

Let $`\mathcal{F}`$ be a family of smooth curves in $`\mathbb{R}^2`$ (the motor primitives). Let $`\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{F}}`$ be the wire plane equipped with the sub-diffeology generated by the family $`\mathcal{F}`$. The inclusion $`\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{F}} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{W}`$ pulls back the equi-affine tensor, so the Two-Thirds Power Law remains intrinsic.

Questions:

1. **Structure of repertoire-generated diffeologies.** Given a finite set $`\mathcal{F}`$, what is the structure of $`\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{F}}`$? Its diffeomorphism group? Its D-topology? Can two different repertoires generate the same sub-diffeology? What geometric invariants distinguish one repertoire from another?

2. **Concatenation as geometry.** Smooth concatenation of curves (via smashing functions [3]) is an operation within any generated diffeology. Does this operation carry an algebraic or categorical structure that formalizes the syntax of motor compositionality?
In particular; Does the sub-diffeology generated by a finite repertoire already contain all smooth concatenations of its primitives? If so, then the geometry generated by a repertoire anticipates every movement that can be built from it — the syntax of motor composition is already inside the geometry. If not, what is the structure of the closure of a generating family under concatenation? Is the merger of two generating families — the union of two repertoires — the geometric operation corresponding to combining motor skills?

4. **Learning as expansion.** Adding a new primitive enlarges $`\mathcal{F}`$. How does $`\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{F}}`$ change? Does the diffeomorphism group grow? Does the D-topology coarsen? Can stages of motor learning be measured by these geometric changes? Does $`\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{F}}`$ converge to the full wire plane as $`\mathcal{F}`$ becomes dense?

5. **Variational principles on sub-diffeologies.** With the equi-affine tensor intrinsic, can one formulate a variational principle directly on $`\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{F}}`$ whose extremals are curves of constant equi-affine speed? What does the calculus of variations look like when the underlying space is not a manifold?

6. **3D and minimum jerk.** In $`\mathbb{R}^3`$, the wire diffeology invariant involves the third derivative (jerk) [1]. Does the sub-diffeology generated by a repertoire of 3D primitives unify the Two-Thirds Power Law (2D) and the minimum jerk model (3D) as aspects of a single geometric structure?

### Conjecture

The motor primitives framework and diffeology are not merely analogous — they are mathematically correspondent. A motor repertoire, in the sense of Flash and colleagues, is a generating family of curves. The geometry of the motor workspace, as experienced and learned by the motor system, is the diffeology generated by that family. The operations on primitives — concatenation, smoothing, selection, addition during learning — are geometric operations on the generating family within this diffeology. The Two-Thirds Power Law is an intrinsic invariant of this geometry, preserved under the expansion of the repertoire.
